"""
@ingroup PATTERN_API
@brief Enumerate the components applied to pattern pieces — everything mounted on the fabric rather than the
fabric itself: buttons, buttonholes, graphics, prints, zippers and trims (buckles, rings, beads, ...).
@param _patternIndex: target pattern index (RealPatternList order, as used by GetPatternCount /
MovePatternsToUVSpace). Pass -1 (the default) for every pattern in the scene.
@param _types: component types to report — any of "button", "buttonhole", "graphic", "print", "zipper",
"trim". Empty (the default) reports every type. An unknown name fails the call.
@return JSON: {"status","patterns":[{"patternIndex","patternName","components":[...]}]}. The response shape is
the same whether one pattern or all were requested — a single pattern comes back as a one-element
"patterns" array. Patterns with nothing applied have an empty "components" array.
"status" is one of "success" or "failed" (the complete set); on "failed" a "message" explains why and
"patterns" is absent.

Component field schema. Every field listed for a type is ALWAYS present on components of that type -
there are no conditional fields - so consumers can read them directly without membership checks.
"Unset" values are signalled in-band (see the field notes) rather than by omitting the key:

type          | fields (in addition to the common four)
--------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------
(every type)  | type, name, uid, patternIndex
button        | styleIndex, position{x,y}, angle
buttonhole    | styleIndex, position{x,y}, angle
graphic       | styleIndex, styleName, position{x,y}, angle, width, height
print         | styleIndex, styleName, position{x,y}, angle, width, height
zipper        | (none - the common four only)
trim          | trimType, styleName

Field notes:
"type"        one of "button", "buttonhole", "graphic", "print", "zipper", "trim".
"uid"         runtime handle, regenerated on load - never persist it between sessions.
"styleIndex"  index into that type's style library (button head / buttonhole / graphic style list,
the same ordering as GetGraphicStyleListWithIndex for graphics). -1 when no style is
assigned or it cannot be resolved.
"styleName"   JSON null when no style is assigned.
"position"    millimetres. NOTE: buttons/buttonholes report 2D-window world coordinates while
graphics/prints report pattern-local coordinates - do not compare the two directly.
"trimType"    e.g. "Buckle", "Ring", "Bead"; "None" when the trim has no type set.
A zipper relates to both patterns its tapes are stitched to, so it is reported under each of them.
"""

"""
@ingroup PATTERN_API
@brief Get details of all patterns and their position on the human body with semantic labels and body region grouping.
Returns a JSON string with two top-level arrays, "upperBody" and "lowerBody", each
containing the pattern objects that belong to that body section.
Each pattern object includes:
- patternName: name of the pattern piece
- patternIndex: index in the real pattern list
- arrangementPosition: internal body region ID (e.g. "Arm_Front_2_L")
- semanticLabel: fine-grained garment part label (e.g. "sleeve", "bodice_front")
- bodyRegion: high-level anatomical region (e.g. "torso_front", "arm_full", "leg_back")
- patternPosition: front/back orientation derived from bodyRegion
("front", "back", "full", "side", "center", or "unknown")

Arrangement position naming convention: {Region}_{Facing}_{Zone}_{Side}
Region : body area        (Arm, Body, Leg, Wrist, Ankle, Neck, Head, Shoulder)
Facing : orientation       (Front, Back, Inside, Outside, Center, Skirt, Calf)
Zone   : vertical segment (1 = closest to torso, 2 = mid, 3 = distal)
Side   : laterality        (L = Left, R = Right; omitted for center-line positions)

Supported semantic labels:
"bodice_front"      - front torso patterns (set-in, raglan, legacy, Adidas)
"bodice_back"       - back torso patterns (set-in, raglan, legacy, Adidas)
"bodice_full"       - full wrap-around torso patterns
"sleeve"            - arm/sleeve patterns (set-in, raglan, dummy)
"cuff"              - wrist cuff patterns
"collar"            - collar/neck patterns (set-in, raglan, Adidas)
"hem"               - bottom hem band of the top
"placket"           - front placket (button/zipper strip)
"waistband"         - waist transition patterns
"pants_front"       - front pants panels
"pants_back"        - back pants panels
"pants_left"        - outer left leg panels
"pants_right"       - outer right leg panels
"pants_front_left"  - front left leg panel
"pants_front_right" - front right leg panel
"pants_back_left"   - back left leg panel
"pants_back_right"  - back right leg panel
"pants_full"        - full leg panel
"skirt_front"       - front skirt patterns
"skirt_back"        - back skirt patterns
"skirt_full"        - full skirt patterns
"cuff_leg"          - ankle cuff patterns
"pocket"            - pocket patterns
"unknown"           - unrecognized or unassigned

Supported body regions:
"torso_front" - front bodice, placket, front jacket pocket blocks
"torso_back"  - back bodice blocks (set-in, raglan, legacy)
"torso_full"  - full wrap-around bodice, hem, Adidas full body, body dummy blocks
"arm_front"   - sleeve blocks (set-in, raglan, dummy)
"arm_full"    - wrist cuff blocks (wraps around)
"leg_front"   - front pants, front-left/right pants, front skirt, pants pocket blocks
"leg_back"    - back pants, back-left/right pants, back skirt blocks
"leg_side"    - outer seam leg panels (left/right)
"leg_full"    - full pants, full skirt, ankle cuff, pants dummy blocks
"neck"        - all collar blocks
"waist"       - waistband blocks

Patterns connected through seamline pairs form a single garment piece; each piece is
classified by majority vote (torso/arm/neck -> upper body, leg/waist -> lower body,
ties default to upper body) and every member is placed in the matching array.

@return JSON string with two array keys, "upperBody" and "lowerBody", each containing
the pattern detail objects for that section. On failure (no pattern editor),
both arrays are empty so the response is always valid, parseable JSON.
"""
